g.text: Three guards, eight combinations — and which one is load-bearing
source required · dedup OR idempotent sink sufficient · 3 of 8 rows reach 45
2 // Two of an event's five fields are CLOCKS, which ch01 established:
3 // et = event time, when it happened · pt = processing time, when we saw it
4 // v = the value being summed (also, here, the amount to charge)
5 type Event { id, key, et, pt, v }
6 // primitive: EVENTS — the book's 9 events, in PROCESSING order (tools/stream_seed.js).
7 // EVENTS[4] = (id 4, key "a", et 245, pt 246, v 6) <- the order this chapter charges
8 // primitive: NONE — no value. Distinct from a value of 0.
9 // primitive: WIN — the window width, in seconds of event time. WIN = 120
10 // primitive: CHK — the index whose state was checkpointed before the crash. CHK = 4
11 // primitive: TOTAL — the dataset's true total. TOTAL = 45
12 // primitive: winOf(et) — the START of the window holding et.
14 // primitive: append(xs, x) — xs with x added at the end. append([1], 2) = [1,2]
15 // primitive: contains(xs, x) — is x in xs? contains([1,2], 2) = true
20 // primitive: REPLAYED — the ids re-read after the crash. REPLAYED = [5, 6, 7, 8]
21 // primitive: REPLAY_V — their combined v. REPLAY_V = 22
23 // function: setRow(sink, w, value) — IDEMPOTENT: names the result.
30 // function: addRow(sink, w, delta) — NOT idempotent: names a change.
37 // primitive: firstN(xs, n) — the first n elements. firstN([1,2,3], 2) = [1,2]
38 // primitive: windowTotal(w, ids) — sum of v over the DISTINCT ids in window w.
40 // primitive: sumRows(sink) — every row added up. sumRows(a full sink) = 45
41 // primitive: verdictOf(t) — "CORRECT" when t == TOTAL, else "LOST" or "DOUBLE".
44 // function: runPipeline(replayable, dedup, idempotent) — one crash, three guards.
53 for (e in EVENTS) { feed = append(feed, e.id) }
55 for (e in REPLAYED) { feed = append(feed, e.id) }
64 if (idempotent) { sink = setRow(sink, w, windowTotal(w, seen)) }
65 if (idempotent == false) { sink = addRow(sink, w, EVENTS[id].v) }
70 // function: main() — THE CALLER: the four interesting rows of the table.
Step 1/0 — dedup drops the replayed record on a membership test
`seen` already holds id 5 from the first pass, so `contains` is true and the replayed copy is skipped before it can reach the sink. `dedupOnly` reaches 45 —
correct, with a sink that merely ADDS. The guard is upstream of the sink's weakness.

Step 2/0 — OR the sink names the result, which makes the repeat harmless
`dedup` is false here, so the replayed id is NOT skipped — it reaches the sink. But `setRow` writes `windowTotal(w, seen)`, the window's total over distinct ids, so
writing it again changes nothing. `idemOnly` also reaches 45. Two different guards, same result: they are redundant for an aggregation.

Step 3/0 — with neither, the add runs twice
`addRow` adds `EVENTS[5].v` = 1 to a row that already contains it. Across all 4 replayed records the total reaches 67 — DOUBLE. Nothing errored; the sink simply
applied a delta it had already applied.

e = NONE (the feed loops are done)
Step 4/0 — and no guard can recover a record that was never re-read
With `replayable` false the feed is truncated to 5 ids BEFORE the loop, so `dedup` and `idempotent` — both true here — never see the missing records. 23, LOST. Both
accuracy guards are subtractive: they stop a contribution counting twice and can do nothing else.
